per_question.question: What is the federal statutory authority for NC's CAP/DA waiver, and what does the state need to demonstrate in its waiver application?
per_question.agent_answer:
NC’s CAP/DA waiver is a **home- and community-based services waiver under section 1915(c) of the Social Security Act**, implemented through the federal HCBS waiver rules in **42 CFR Part 441, Subpart G**. The NC CAP/DA policy itself reflects that framework by requiring a **nursing-facility level of care**, a signed service plan, the ability to remain safely in the community, and that paid care needs stay within the **average institutional cost** of the waiver. [42 CFR Part 441](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-441); [Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

## Federal authority

For a 1915(c) HCBS waiver application, the governing federal regulation says the waiver request must include:

- the required **state assurances** and supporting documentation;
- any requested waivers of statewideness, comparability, or certain medically needy rules when applicable; and
- a statement about whether the state will refuse HCBS where community costs would exceed the cost of equivalent institutional care.  
  [42 CFR Part 441, § 441.301](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-441)

That means the relevant federal authority for CAP/DA is **section 1915(c)**, not the public-notice rule in 42 CFR 431.408. The public-notice rule may apply to certain demonstration projects, but the substantive HCBS waiver application requirements here are in **42 CFR Part 441**. I could not verify the underlying Social Security Act text itself in this corpus, but the federal regulations retrieved clearly treat this as a **1915(c) waiver**. [42 CFR Part 441](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-441)

## What the state must demonstrate in its waiver application

Under the federal HCBS waiver rules, the state must provide **satisfactory assurances** and enough supporting documentation for CMS to approve the waiver.

### 1. Required assurances
The state must assure CMS, among other things, that:

- necessary **health and welfare safeguards** protect beneficiaries;
- provider standards are adequate;
- state licensure/certification requirements are met;
- services are provided in **home and community-based settings**;
- the state maintains an **incident management system**; and
- there is **financial accountability** for waiver funds.  
  [42 CFR Part 441, § 441.302](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-441)

### 2. Supporting documentation
The state must furnish enough information to support those assurances, including at minimum:

- a description of safeguards protecting health and welfare;
- provider qualification standards;
- administrative oversight mechanisms for quality of care;
- records and information supporting **financial accountability** and an audit trail;
- the plan for **evaluation and reevaluation** of level of care, including who performs it, what instrument is used, and the reevaluation intervals;
- the plan for informing beneficiaries of **feasible alternatives** and allowing them to choose institutional care or HCBS; and
- documentation of **free choice of providers** and fair-hearing protections.  
  [42 CFR Part 441, § 441.353](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-441)

### 3. Service and eligibility design the application must describe
The waiver request must also show that services will be:

- furnished under a **written person-centered service plan** approved by the Medicaid agency;
- limited to people who are **not institutional inpatients**; and
- limited to people who, **without HCBS, would require Medicaid-covered institutional level of care** such as nursing-facility care.  
  It also must describe the target group, the qualifications of the people developing the plan of care, and define each waiver service separately. [42 CFR Part 441, § 441.301](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-441)

## How NC’s CAP/DA policy reflects those federal requirements

NC’s current CAP/DA clinical policy is consistent with that 1915(c) structure. It says CAP/DA coverage requires, among other things, that the beneficiary:

- meets the required **HCBS nursing facility level of care**;
- has a completed CAP assessment showing a reasonable indication of need for waiver services;
- has a signed service plan authorizing waiver services;
- can maintain health, safety, and well-being in the home or approved setting with supports; and
- has paid care needs that can be maintained within the **average institutional cost** of the CAP/DA waiver.  
  [Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA), § 3.2.1, eff. Sept. 1, 2025](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

## Amendment status

I checked amendments for both cited documents:

- **42 CFR Part 441**: I did **not** retrieve amendment history for this document in this answer, so I cannot represent its amendment status beyond the section text retrieved from the current eCFR link.
- **CAP/DA Policy 3K-2**: amendment check returned no separate amendments in the corpus, and the policy appears current with an effective date of **Sept. 1, 2025**. [Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

## Bottom line

- **Federal statutory authority:** **section 1915(c) of the Social Security Act**, implemented in **42 CFR Part 441, Subpart G**.  
- **What NC must demonstrate in its waiver application:** satisfactory assurances and documentation showing **health and welfare protections, provider standards, financial accountability, level-of-care evaluation, person-centered planning, beneficiary choice/free choice of providers, and that participants would otherwise require institutional care**.
